note: Eighteen curated links supplied by the curator. Every URL was fetched and returned HTTP 200, and the headline, publication date and outlet are taken from the page's own metadata rather than from the URL slug or from a summary. Where the URL date and the published date disagreed the metadata was used: the Los Angeles Times pieces at 2026-05-06 and 2026-08-03 in their URLs publish as 2026-05-07 and 2026-08-04. AMP and tracking parameters were stripped from the URLs before storing.

replace.reason: Batch 149 added this story from KPBS, which carries it as a syndicated copy. The curator has now supplied the NPR original, which is added here, so the KPBS duplicate is removed rather than leaving the same headline in the newswire twice.

skipped.reason: Two reasons, either of which is enough. The fetch was refused so the headline and date could not be verified, and the URL dates the piece to June 24, 2024 — before the dashboard tracker start of May 7, 2025. The newswire filters to the tracker window, so this link would have been created successfully and then never appeared.

The fetch was refused, so the headline and publication date could not be read from the page. A 403 means the request was blocked, not that the article is gone — it can be added by hand from the admin, or supplied with its headline and date and it will go in.

same_story_note: Some of these cover one another. The Mercury News piece of July 23 and the Los Angeles Times piece of July 22 appear to be the same cinder-block sentencing; the Los Angeles Magazine, Ventura County Star and Los Angeles Times items about a Westlake man and a CHP car may be one defendant across three outlets. Several outlets on one story is normal in a newswire and none is removed, but it is worth knowing before the feed is read as a count of separate cases.
